notes: Consolidated from four one-function sources by tools/tubuild.py create and then rewritten by hand: the shadow banner was replaced with a real file comment, the generator's extern "C" wrapper around the enter-table externs was dropped (a namespace-scope variable is not mangled, so the block was inert), and SetState's `mRender = data_02086b58;` became `mRender = 0;` -- mwccarm lowers a null pointer-to-member assignment to a reference to arm9's __ptmf_null at 0x02086b58 itself, so the address literal was carrying no information the compiler did not already supply. All four functions still byte-match.

dMgState_c is a COINED class name. tools/rtti_extract.py recovers 429 RTTI records from the cartridge and none of them names it, flat or nested -- the probe does see nested spellings (dMgPsOpt_c::TouchIcon_c, dScMgBase_c::graphCallback_c and dScMgSlot1_c::betIcon_c are all in the same extraction), so the absence is a measurement, not a blind spot. The class is non-polymorphic: no base, no virtual member, no _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS emitted by the object and none configured at any address in any symbols.txt. A coined name only blocks promotion when the TU emits RTTI whose home would have to be licensed under the coined spelling, so it does not block here.

This TU is NOT text-only production. SetState owns a function-local static array and its guard word, and tools/objisolate.py plan_many refuses any surviving non-.text section: 'unlicensed content in text-only multi-symbol object: section[5] .bss size 0x4 defines [...]; section[6] .bss size 0xa0 defines [...]'. One-function production isolation escapes that by externalising the two statics, which is why the per-function shard linked and why ov004's symbols.txt carries names for them at all; the multi-symbol path has no externalise step. Hence production_mode intact-object with an explicit .bss claim at 0x020bfd04..0x020bfda8 -- 0x4 for the guard and 0xa0 for twenty 8-byte pointer-to-member slots, ending exactly where ov004's next configured bss symbol begins. Nothing outside this TU reaches those bytes: the only two relocations to them in ov004's relocs.txt come from 0x020b8a14 and 0x020b8a1c, both inside SetState.

The $NN suffix on the two statics is a per-TU mwccarm counter, and it is reconstruction-dependent rather than cartridge evidence -- a Nintendo DS cartridge carries no symbol table. Measured on this tree: SetState compiled alone with only the enter-table externs lands on $19, which is the spelling ov004's symbols.txt was given when the one-function shard was matched; adding the ApproachLinear declaration moves it to $22, adding the constructor to $23, and the whole consolidated TU to $26. No source form of a four-function TU can reach 19, so $19 is an artifact of the shard rather than a property of the original translation unit. This entry licenses the consolidated TU's own $26 spellings.

BLOCKED SHORT OF PRODUCTION, and the refusals are the tools' own. Three routes were measured on this candidate. (1) Text-only multi-symbol production: tools/objisolate.py plan_many refuses 'unlicensed content in text-only multi-symbol object: section[5] .bss size 0x4 defines [_ZGVsEnterTable$26]; section[6] .bss size 0xa0 defines [sEnterTable$26]; section[13] .text size 0x1c defines [_ZN10dMgState_cC2Ev]'. (2) Text-only plus a compiler-only deadstrip that re-imports the two statics the way one-function isolation does: 'compiler-only deadstrip refused: surviving section[10] .text references compiler-only data _ZGVsEnterTable$26 at 0x234; only _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS may be imported this way'. (3) The intact-object route recorded above, which LINKS: 4/4 licensed functions byte-identical in the linked image, 106/106 modules exact at 100.000000%, objectAudit LICENSED 6/6 with no non-licensed symbol and no unlicensed section, and a full ROM byte-identical to the strict stock control. Its only failure is dsd check symbols --fail, 6 new lines over the tree's 9 pre-existing ones, all four naming the same two bss addresses: data_ov004_020bfd04 and data_ov004_020bfd08 are no longer in the linked binary once the TU supplies those bytes (dsd itself offers _ZGVsEnterTable$26 and sEnterTable$26 as the replacement names), and _ZGVsEnterTable$19 and sEnterTable$19 are 'expected to be global but is local'.

What would clear it, and why it cannot be done from here. The two statics need a second spelling at the same storage so the pre-promotion one-function source and the post-promotion TU can both resolve: the shard emits and externalises $19, the consolidated TU emits $26, and ov004's symbols.txt can serve exactly one of them. That is the storage-alias feature, and rombuild.py refuses it in as many words -- 'automatic intact-object storage aliases are not supported until baseline bootstrapping is non-circular'. Editing symbols.txt instead makes the change atomic with the promotion, and the proof harness cannot straddle it: rombuild.intact_tu_policies requires linkcheck.symbolCheckNewVsBaseline to be empty against a baseline control, and 'tubuild.py linkcheck --baseline' does no TU substitution, so with the rows re-pointed it dies on the still-enrolled shard with "Error: Failed to delink 'src/_ZN10dMgState_c8SetStateEi.cpp'". Next action: either storage aliases land, or a promotion path that accepts a symbols.txt re-point as part of the same change. Everything else about this TU is proved.

compiler_only_output.reason: dMgState_c has no virtual bases and no virtual functions, so mwccarm emits the C1 complete-object constructor and the identical C2 base-object variant from the one written definition. The cartridge kept only C1 (ov004:0x020b8a70); nothing constructs a dMgState_c as a base subobject, so the retail link discarded C2 and no configured symbol in any of the 106 symbols.txt files names it. Homeless, therefore a plain deadstrip rather than deadstrip-duplicate; tools/tubuild.py all_symbol_homes() returns None for it.
